title: Heat Pump Rebates in Kitchener 2026: Program Rebates and a Free Energy Coach
desc: Kitchener heat pump rebates for 2026 under Home Renovation Savings, plus the Region's free Energy Coach and why the RetrofitWR loan does not reach Kitchener.
badge: Up to $7,500 for an air-source heat pump
lead: Kitchener has 99,815 households. The heat pump rebate is $500 or $1,250 per ton by current fuel, and Waterloo Region offers free coaching to help you choose.
cards_heading: What Home Renovation Savings pays for a heat pump in Kitchener
cards_intro: We re-read the program's heat pump page and its requirements document on October 3, 2026. No home energy assessment is needed for this stream, but a participating HVAC contractor and written pre-approval are.

cards.title: Air-source, electric, oil, propane or wood heat
cards.note: For a cold-climate air-source heat pump replacing electric resistance, oil, propane or wood as the main heat. A 3-ton system pays $3,750 and 6 tons or more reaches the cap.

cards.title: Air-source, Enbridge gas heat
cards.note: For homes primarily heated by an Enbridge gas furnace or boiler. The cap is reached at 4 tons.

cards.title: Ground-source
cards.note: For electric, oil, propane or wood homes. Gas homes get a flat $3,000. The system must be a full installation sized to the home's load.

cards.title: Rented heat pump
cards.note: Rentals are eligible for any primary heating fuel: $500 per ton for air-source, up to $2,000, or a flat $3,000 for ground-source.

cards.title: More than one outdoor unit
cards.amount: Up to three units, one rebate
cards.note: If several outdoor units are needed to heat the whole home, their tons add up and one rebate is paid on the total, for example 3 + 3 tons for $7,500.

cards.title: One rebate, pre-approved
cards.note: One rebate per home. The contractor needs written pre-approval before installing, files the post-installation application within 30 days, and the cheque arrives within 60 days of approval.

after_cards: The requirements document lists no end date, but the program's other streams close in late 2026, so check the program page before you sign a contract. Pre-approval is mandatory: an installation done first earns nothing.
sections: The 2021 Census counts 47% of Kitchener households in detached houses, 66% in an eligible type and 60% owning. 21,465 are owner-occupied detached houses built before 1981. 15% live in low-rise apartments and 3,155 in duplexes. 4.7% report needing major repairs.

Retrofit Waterloo Region's free Energy Coach is open to homeowners across the Region. Its loan, up to $40,000 at 2.5% over 10 or 15 years, is repaid on the GrandBridge Energy bill and is limited to customers in Cambridge and North Dumfries. Kitchener is served by Enova Power, so the loan does not apply. A coach can help you decide between ductless and central systems before you ask for quotes.

The owner must own the home and pay for the installation. Where an owner has tenants, the owner applies, and a tenant cannot apply on the owner's behalf. A Kitchener landlord with a rented upper unit should confirm that the home qualifies as an eligible type and has a central heating system before applying.

The program accepts centrally ducted, partially ducted and ductless cold-climate systems, including single-head and multi-head mini-splits. A multi-head system must still meet the whole-home heating requirement. Ask the contractor to show how many indoor heads are planned and which rooms they cover.

The work order has to be fully itemized in the format of the program's sample invoice. For a ground-source system it must also show the loop design and the closed-loop heating capacity on which the rebate is calculated.
claim_steps: Book a free coaching session with the Region if you want a second opinion.
Confirm eligibility on the program's short form and get the list of participating HVAC contractors.
Choose a contractor from that list. Ask for a load calculation and the NRCan sizing tool form for each outdoor unit.
Wait for written pre-approval before any installation starts.
After the install, check that the contractor files the post-installation application within 30 days, with the final itemized invoice and photos.
faq: Can Kitchener use the RetrofitWR loan?
No. It is for GrandBridge customers in Cambridge and North Dumfries.
Yes, for homeowners across the Region.
